authored.summary: The five Ichimoku lines with the cloud projected ahead of price, shaded green or red by which leading span is on top
authored.description:
## What it shows
Five lines on the price chart, each the midpoint of the highest high and lowest low over a window. The **Conversion line** uses **Conversion line length** bars (9 by default) and the **Base line** **Base line length** bars (26). **Leading span A** is the midpoint of those two and **Leading span B** uses **Leading span B length** bars (52); both are drawn ahead of the bar that computed them, and the **Lagging span** — the close — is drawn behind it, each by one bar less than **Displacement** (26 by default, so 25 bars). The cloud between the leading spans is green where span A is above span B and red where it is below.

## How to read it
- Price above the cloud is read as an up trend, below it as a down trend, and inside it as undecided.
- A thick cloud ahead marks strong support or resistance; a thin one is easier to break.
- The conversion line crossing the base line is the classic early signal; it carries more weight on the right side of the cloud.
- Alerts are available for **Close crossed above the cloud**, **Close crossed below the cloud**, **Conversion crossed above base** and **Conversion crossed below base**. The cloud alerts judge the close against the cloud drawn over its own bar.

## Limits
- Leading span B needs **Leading span B length** bars before it is drawn, so the full cloud appears only after that.
- The lines are built from highs and lows only; the lagging span is the close moved back, not a forecast.
- In a sideways market price drifts in and out of a thin cloud and the signals whip.
